description: The average number of orders per account counts only accounts that have orders.

d.request: For accounts with standing orders, compute the average orders per account; identify accounts exceeding this average; for each, display account_id, order count, its excess over the average, and its excess over the average of above-average accounts; sort by the last metric descending, showing the top 10.
d.sql: WITH order_counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) as order_count FROM `order` GROUP BY account_id), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) as avg_orders FROM order_counts), above_average AS (SELECT oc.account_id, oc.order_count, oa.avg_orders, oc.order_count - oa.avg_orders as excess_over_avg FROM order_counts oc CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa WHERE oc.order_count > oa.avg_orders), above_avg_stats AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) as above_avg_mean FROM above_average) SELECT aa.account_id, aa.order_count, ROUND(aa.excess_over_avg, 2) as excess_over_average, ROUND(aa.order_count - aas.above_avg_mean, 2) as excess_over_above_avg_mean FROM above_average aa CROSS JOIN above_avg_stats aas ORDER BY aa.order_count - aas.above_avg_mean DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: For each account with standing orders (`order.account_id`), count its orders. Work out the average number of orders per account, using only accounts that have at least one order. Keep the accounts whose order count is above that average. For each, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of the kept above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest and return only the first 10 rows. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH order_counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM `order` GROUP BY account_id), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) as overall_avg_val FROM order_counts), filtered_accounts AS (SELECT oc.account_id, oc.cnt FROM order_counts oc CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa WHERE oc.cnt > oa.overall_avg_val), filtered_avg AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) as filtered_avg_val FROM filtered_accounts) SELECT fa.account_id, fa.cnt, fa.cnt - oa.overall_avg_val, fa.cnt - fa2.filtered_avg_val FROM filtered_accounts fa CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa CROSS JOIN filtered_avg fa2 ORDER BY (fa.cnt - fa2.filtered_avg_val) DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: For each account with standing orders (`order.account_id`), count its orders. Which accounts have more orders than the average number of orders per account? For each, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of those above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest and give only the first 10. Don't round anything. The average number of orders per account counts only accounts that have orders.
c.sql:
WITH account_order_counts AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) as order_count
  FROM "order"
  GROUP BY account_id
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) as avg_orders
  FROM account_order_counts
),
above_average_accounts AS (
  SELECT aoc.account_id, aoc.order_count
  FROM account_order_counts aoc
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
  WHERE aoc.order_count > oa.avg_orders
),
above_average_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) as avg_above_average
  FROM above_average_accounts
)
SELECT 
  aaa.account_id,
  aaa.order_count,
  aaa.order_count - oa.avg_orders as above_overall_avg,
  aaa.order_count - aaa_avg.avg_above_average as above_above_avg
FROM above_average_accounts aaa
CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
CROSS JOIN above_average_avg aaa_avg
ORDER BY aaa.order_count - aaa_avg.avg_above_average DESC
LIMIT 10

b.request: For accounts with at least one order, find those with order counts exceeding the mean orders per such account, then report each account's ID, order count, how far above the overall mean, and how far above the mean of above-average accounts, sorted by the latter metric descending, showing the top 10.
b.sql:
WITH order_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    account_id,
    COUNT(*) as order_count
  FROM `order`
  GROUP BY account_id
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) as mean_orders FROM order_counts
),
above_average_with_mean AS (
  SELECT 
    oc.account_id,
    oc.order_count,
    om.mean_orders
  FROM order_counts oc
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
  WHERE oc.order_count > om.mean_orders
),
above_average_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) as mean_above_avg
  FROM above_average_with_mean
)
SELECT 
  aawm.account_id,
  aawm.order_count,
  aawm.order_count - aawm.mean_orders as above_overall_mean,
  aawm.order_count - aam.mean_above_avg as above_above_avg_mean
FROM above_average_with_mean aawm
CROSS JOIN above_average_mean aam
ORDER BY above_above_avg_mean DESC
LIMIT 10
